memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When he caught up with them, he repeated these words to them. But they said to him, 'Why does my lord say such things? Far be it from your servants to do anything like that! We even brought back to you from the land of Canaan the silver we found inside the mouths of our sacks. So why would we steal silver or gold from your master's house? If any of your servants is found to have it, he will die; and the rest of us will become my lord's slaves.'" — Gen 44:6-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The brothers are genuinely offended — and genuinely honest. They point to their own record: we brought the silver back, why would we steal now? These are not the same men who once sold a brother for twenty pieces of silver. Something has changed in them.

But look at how confidently they speak. "If any of your servants is found to have it, he will die." They are so sure of their innocence that they pronounce a sentence on themselves. It is easy to speak boldly about a sin you are certain you have not committed.

Peter did something similar. "Even if all fall away, I will not" (Mk 14:29). Confidence in our own standing is a fragile thing. The moment we say "I would never," we have stepped onto ground we cannot hold up on our own.

The healthier posture is honest humility. Not "I could never fall," but "Lord, keep me." Not "I am innocent," but "search me, God, and know my heart" (Ps 139:23-24). Real growth had happened in these men, and God saw it. But their safety never rested on their own strength — and neither does ours. We stand only because He holds us (Jude 24).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where are you most confident that you would never fall? Is that confidence in yourself or in God?
2. How has God changed you in an area where you once failed badly?
3. What would it look like to ask God to search your heart today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for the ways You have already changed me. Keep me from proud confidence in my own strength. Search my heart, hold me firm, and let me stand only in You. Amen.
